guest.bio_context: Zach Billings has spent his entire career focused on one problem: getting dealers noticed online. He leads Wikimotive, a company that has been operating for over two decades and is widely recognized by dealership owners. His work centers on understanding how AI-powered search engines like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude rank and recommend car dealerships based on content quality, reviews, and inventory visibility.

pending_qa.q: What is the difference between ranking factors for Google's local business map pack versus traditional organic SEO results?
pending_qa.r: Location is the primary ranking factor for the map pack—unless a dealership moves physically closer to where consumers are searching, they cannot materially change their map pack position. A consumer typing 'Ford dealer near me' will see the closest dealership first, second closest second, and so on. However, dealerships can handicap themselves by leaving their Google Business Profile incomplete, missing categories, wrong hours, or incorrect information. Assuming all that is filled out, location dominates the ranking.

pending_qa.q: How do dealer groups with multiple locations gain competitive advantage in AI search visibility?
pending_qa.r: Dealer groups can pool inventory across all their websites, and more inventory is a huge lever for both AI search and traditional search. When someone searches 'F-150 for sale near me,' the entity with the most F-150s is the most logical choice independent of content quality. Groups often win by default because they have so much inventory they outweigh single-point dealerships in opportunity to show up in searches. If an owner consolidates around one brand like Ford with four or five stores, they naturally show up most prominently for that brand in their region.

pending_qa.q: What percentage of dealership consumer search volume currently comes from AI platforms versus traditional search?
pending_qa.r: Literally 99% of the available market share for low funnel dealership opportunity is from traditional search, not AI search at this point. AI search is evolving and growing, but the disproportionate focus on AI search optimizations means many dealers are focusing resources on something that represents only about 1% of consumer market share that dealerships can buy for, while ignoring the other 99% that remains in traditional search paid and organic.

pending_qa.q: Why is Google Performance Max campaign automation becoming increasingly wasteful for car dealerships?
pending_qa.r: Performance Max campaigns ask dealerships to drop money into a bucket, and Google returns intended outcomes. The problem is that if John Smith Chevrolet uses Performance Max, Google will show ads for the cheapest way to get leads—which is simply showing up when someone Googles 'John Smith Chevrolet' directly. This wastes spend on branded search rather than driving high-intent consumers who are actually shopping for vehicles. While Pmax is designed to maximize performance, it often maximizes the wrong performance metric for dealerships.
